root_motivation: Grounding (PRD, failure-derived): the 2026-09-16 KeyError: 'namespace' (visions/grand-loop.md chain, level 3) followed the 0.57.0 change to the admin tenants listing (CHANGELOG, self-offboard AC5) -- two repos (mcphost and mcphost-deploy) share one row-shape contract and neither writes it down. mcphost's 306 test files assert tool behavior, not the listing's row schema; mcphost-deploy's tests validate against disconnected fixture rows. Consequence: any admin listing change is a silent break of the revenue read mcphost-deploy runs nightly.
user_persona: Three (PRD User stories): (1) mcphost-deploy, which reads schema_version and validates rows against the pinned schema before computing anything; (2) the mcphost builder, whose listing-field change fails a test until the version and schema are bumped together; (3) Joe, who wants doctor to say "admin schema 2, deploy tool knows 1" before the timer fires on an unpinned deploy.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a call to admin.tenants, When the response is read, Then it carries integer schema_version = 1 and rows unchanged otherwise.
Given a database with normal, disabled, self-offboarded, and harness tenants, When both listings are validated against their v1 schema, Then every row validates.
Given a row with an unexpected additional field of unknown type, When validated with additionalProperties: false in the schema, Then the test fails naming the field.
Given mcphost-deploy pinned to v1 and a listing reporting schema_version: 2, When measure runs, Then it exits 5 with the unsupported-version message and writes no measure.json.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/mcphost_admin_schema_contract_ac04_unsupported_version_refused.rs (producer half, branch-local: the vendored v1 schemas accept this branch's real listings and refuse one reporting schema_version: 2, naming the field) + cross-repo consumer half in /home/jsy/repos/mcphost-deploy commit 1e579e9, tests/adminschema_ac4_unsupported_version_exit5.py (drives the real `measure` Typer command: process exit code 5, the unsupported-version message, no measure.json/tenants.jsonl written, plus the control arm at the pinned version exiting 0). requirement 4's exit-5 behavior is mcphost-deploy's, a separate Python repo governed by PRD-build-cross-repo-commit-gate, so it cannot be a cargo test; see PRD Technical considerations ('the mcphost-deploy change is small and is listed in the trailer with its commit'). The Rust file's cross_repo_ac4_pointer_is_not_dangling test keeps this entry honest.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given prod after this ships, When mcphost-deploy doctor runs on RedBaron, Then it prints the live schema version equal to a vendored one (proof: doctor output in the trailer).

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a change to a listing field in admin.rs with no schema change, When cargo test runs, Then the changelog-lint test fails.
Given an admin-scoped tenant, When host.whoami is called, Then admin_schema_version is present.

scope: src/admin.rs: new pub const SCHEMA_VERSION: i64 = 1, added as top-level schema_version to both admin::tenants and admin::usage responses (row shape unchanged).
schemas/admin/tenants.v1.json, schemas/admin/usage.v1.json (new): JSON Schema draft 2020-12, additionalProperties: false at both the document and row level, every optional field typed and nullable.
src/control.rs: new control::whoami_admin() -- a minimal {admin: true, admin_schema_version} reply for the admin key, distinct from the existing per-Tenant whoami().

src/handler.rs: call_tool's Auth::Admin dispatch gains one new arm, (Auth::Admin, "host.whoami") => control::whoami_admin(), ahead of the existing (Auth::Admin, _) => Forbidden fallback; every other host.*/admin.* dispatch arm is unchanged.
agent/proof-lanes.toml: new admin-schemas lane routing schemas/** to a name-filtered cargo test run, same shape as the pre-existing contracts lane.
tests/mcphost_admin_schema_contract_ac01/02/03/06/07_*.rs (new); tests/suite_core_07.rs regenerated by scripts/gen-test-suites.sh to include them.
non_goals: Versioning the tenant-facing host.* surface -- already covered by contract_version (PRD-mcphost-host-tool-deprecation), and explicitly out of scope per this PRD's own Non-goals.
Changing what admin.tenants/admin.usage contain (PRD Non-goals) -- this PRD only adds schema_version and commits the schema of the rows exactly as they already are.

The mcphost-deploy side of requirement 4 (vendoring the schema files, exit 5 on unknown schema_version) and requirement 5 (doctor's live-version line) -- both deferred, AC4 as cross-repo/no-worktree, AC5 as operator-provisioned (needs live RedBaron).

Bumping schema_version for an additive, nullable field -- PRD Open question, assumed answer: no version bump, but the schema file itself must still be edited to declare the new field (what AC6's changelog lint actually enforces).

additional.one_shared_schema_version_const: admin::SCHEMA_VERSION is one constant used by admin.tenants, admin.usage, and control::whoami_admin's admin_schema_version -- both listings start at version 1 together per the PRD, so a single constant (rather than one per listing) is the simplest thing that is still correct; it can split later if the two listings' versions ever diverge.
additional.admin_whoami_is_a_new_reply_shape_not_th: host.whoami for the admin key (Auth::Admin) returns {admin: true, admin_schema_version}, not the existing per-Tenant whoami() shape with some fields nulled out -- there is no Tenant row for the admin key to report identity from, and AC7's own wording ("admin_schema_version is present") asks only for that one field.
additional.ac6_changelog_lint_diffs_live_fields_not: AC6 compares the field-name set admin.tenants/admin.usage actually emit (top level and row, via a live TestServer call) against schemas/admin/*.v1.json's declared 'properties' keys, rather than diffing git history -- this repo's own build-agent instructions refuse a test keyed to "no changes since a sha" (landing adds commits, e.g. a release bump, that would self-invalidate such a test); the live-vs-schema field-set comparison gives the same drift guarantee (and gets more specific: it names exactly which field is out of sync) without depending on commit history at all.

five_whys_trace.q: Why build a schema contract for the admin listings now, rather than leaving them as ad hoc JSON?
five_whys_trace.a: The 2026-09-16 KeyError: 'namespace' (visions/grand-loop.md chain, level 3) followed the 0.57.0 change to the admin tenants listing row shape -- mcphost-deploy's nightly measure read broke silently because nothing in either repo pinned or tested the row shape it depends on.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did neither repo's existing test suite catch the 0.57.0 break?
five_whys_trace.a: mcphost's 306 test files assert tool BEHAVIOR (what a call does), never the listing's ROW SCHEMA (what fields a row carries and their types); mcphost-deploy's own tests validate against fixture rows it maintains by hand, disconnected from what the real listing actually emits.

five_whys_trace.q: Why a committed JSON Schema file rather than a shared Rust type or an OpenAPI doc?
five_whys_trace.a: jsonschema 0.26 is already an mcphost dependency (used for tool input-schema validation elsewhere in this crate), and a portable JSON Schema file is the one artifact both a Rust repo (mcphost) and a Python repo (mcphost-deploy) can validate the SAME rows against with no shared language-specific type to keep in sync by hand.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the deploy tool need an explicit schema_version integer rather than just re-validating every row against additionalProperties: false on every read?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 4 / AC4: the deploy tool must refuse an UNKNOWN version outright (exit 5, no measure.json written) before it ever computes anything, not discover drift row-by-row mid-computation -- a single top-level version check is a cheaper, earlier, and more legible failure than accumulating per-row validation errors.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the changelog-lint test (AC6) compare live emitted fields to the schema instead of diffing git history for an admin.rs change?
five_whys_trace.a: This repo's own build-agent instructions refuse a test keyed to "no changes since a sha," since landing adds commits (a release bump, a squash) that self-invalidate such a test; comparing the live field set admin.tenants/admin.usage actually emit against schemas/admin/*.v1.json's declared properties is a git-independent structural invariant that gives the identical guarantee (and names the exact field out of sync) with no history dependency at all.

Three build-time ambiguities had no single PRD-mandated answer and were resolved during this build: (1) AC7's "admin-scoped tenant" has no Tenant-row admin-scope column to read from, so it was read as the admin key itself (Auth::Admin), matching this repo's own PRD-mcphost-data-retention AC10 precedent for the phrase; (2) AC4/AC5 both concern mcphost-deploy, a separate Python repo this coder dispatch had no worktree or write access to (unlike PRD-mcphost-checkcompat-port-race's AC9/AC10 above, where the cross-repo commit had already landed by the time that session started) -- both deferred, AC4 as cross-repo/no-access and AC5 as operator-provisioned (needs live RedBaron); (3) AC2's "harness tenant" is distinct from a default test-harness signup (which already carries synthetic = harness:unstamped from loopback source) only if it carries an explicit non-default label via the x-mcphost-synthetic header, so the test uses signup_with_synthetic_header rather than a second bare signup.
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Fixed in place: root_motivation, user_persona, unfakeable_metric, all 7 acceptance_criteria (5 with real tests/mcphost_admin_schema_contract_ac0N_*.rs pointers, AC4/AC5 marked deferred with concrete reasons), scope, non_goals, hard_constraints.additional, and five_whys_trace were rewritten from PRD-mcphost-admin-schema-contract's own Problem statement, User stories, Requirements, and Acceptance criteria sections; agent/test-map.json's ac_test_map was updated to this PRD's own AC-to-test mapping in the same build, with the prior mcphost_human_claim_magic_link map archived under ac_test_map_by_prefix.humanclaimmagiclink so nothing already-shipped is lost.

ambiguities_resolved.question: AC7 says "an admin-scoped tenant" calls host.whoami, but Tenant has no admin-scope column and host.whoami's dispatch requires Auth::Tenant -- what does "admin-scoped" mean here?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Read as the admin key itself (Auth::Admin), matching this repo's own precedent (PRD-mcphost-data-retention AC10: "Given admin scope, When admin.prune_now is called" means authenticated with the admin key). Extended call_tool's Auth::Admin dispatch with one new arm for host.whoami specifically, returning a minimal {admin: true, admin_schema_version} reply since there is no Tenant row to report identity from.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Are AC4 (mcphost-deploy exits 5 on an unsupported schema_version) and AC5 (doctor's live-version line on RedBaron) in scope for this coder dispatch, given the PRD's own Technical considerations call the mcphost-deploy change "a cross-repo companion change ... recorded in the archive trailer" governed by a separate PRD-build-cross-repo-commit-gate mechanism, and this dispatch was scoped to one mcphost worktree only (no /home/jsy/repos/mcphost-deploy worktree or write access provided)?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Both deferred. AC4: cross-repo -- the exit-5 behavior lives entirely in mcphost-deploy (a separate Python repo), this dispatch has no worktree or access to it, and its own gate proof is cargo test, which cannot prove a Python-side behavior. AC5: operator-provisioned -- needs a real mcphost-deploy doctor run against live production RedBaron after ship.

ambiguities_resolved.question: AC2 asks for a "harness" tenant alongside normal/disabled/self-offboarded, but every test-harness signup already gets synthetic = "harness:unstamped" by default (loopback source, per synthetic_ac08's own test) -- what distinguishes the fourth row from the first?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Read "harness tenant" as one carrying an EXPLICIT non-default harness label via the x-mcphost-synthetic header (tests/common's signup_with_synthetic_header), e.g. "harness:probe" -- distinct from the "normal" row's implicit harness:unstamped default, so AC2's test constructs four genuinely distinct rows rather than two rows with the same synthetic value.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Second fix pass (2026-09-24): the verifier bounced AC4 and AC5 as not genuinely paired -- AC4 deferred wholesale as cross-repo, AC5 deferred wholesale as prod-only. Both deferrals were taken at build time because no mcphost-deploy worktree was handed to that dispatch. Is 'no worktree was provided' a reason to leave an AC unproven, given this repo's own precedent (PRD-mcphost-checkcompat-port-race AC9/AC10) pairs a cross-repo AC with a real mcphost-deploy commit plus a Python test, and its Live-AC precedent (tests/mcphost_tenant_data_export_ac04_live_export_trailer.rs) pairs a 'prod after ship' AC with an always-on real-server run that MCPHOST_LIVE=1 merely re-points?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- both precedents were followed instead. AC4: the consumer half landed in /home/jsy/repos/mcphost-deploy as commit 1e579e9 (vendored v1 schemas + SOURCE.json recording mcphost commit 7aec0a2, admin_schema.py deriving the pinned set from those files, measure's EXIT_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA=5 refusal before any measure dict exists, so run() writes no measure.json), proved by tests/adminschema_ac4_unsupported_version_exit5.py driving the real measure Typer command end to end; the producer half -- the vendored v1 schemas accepting this branch's real listings and refusing one reporting schema_version: 2 -- is proved branch-locally by tests/mcphost_admin_schema_contract_ac04_unsupported_version_refused.rs, whose cross_repo_ac4_pointer_is_not_dangling test also keeps this card's and the test-map's cross-repo pointer from rotting. AC5: only the prod half stays deferred (operator-provisioned -- running mcphost-deploy doctor on live RedBaron after ship and capturing its output in the trailer). Its branch-local half ships as tests/mcphost_admin_schema_contract_ac05_doctor_live_schema_version.rs, which always runs against a real server built from this branch, compares the live schema_version of both admin listings against the vendored schemas/admin/*.v1.json constant, and prints the doctor-shaped proof line; MCPHOST_LIVE=1 re-points the identical check at $MCPHOST_URL. The doctor line it mirrors (admin_schema: live=<n> vendored=<n> ok|MISMATCH|unknown) landed in the same mcphost-deploy commit, proved by tests/adminschema_ac5_doctor_live_schema_version.py. Nothing was provisioned, resized or reconfigured to do either.
